answer: Under bonded escrow, correlated equivocation by k identities is treated as a coordinated fault, with penalties scaling as O(k²) rather than as k separate fines. Upon detection, an additional exponential multiplier increases capital loss as the swarm grows; asymmetric depreciation further reduces the value of returned collateral. Splitting one operator across mirror identities therefore does not avoid the penalty ridge: each linked thread of evidence can expose the larger coalition and its compounded liability.
